messages:
sara: Quick check — can someone run a short nsys + torch.profiler smoke for the kvcache warmup regression on llama2-13b-qat? Seeing ~20% higher cold-start p99 on batch=4 after the last kernel swap.

 dave: I can do a run today. Which exact commit + model build? also need the input prompt set you used.

 sara: repro commit is `main@f3a9c7b` (the kernel-allocator change). Prompt set: 10 short prompts in tests/bench/warmup_prompts.txt (mostly <64 tokens). Use sequence length 256, batch=4, temperature=0.

 anjali: pinging perf-bot to remind about trace size limits and redaction checklist :eyes:

 perf-bot: Reminder — upload traces to s3://perf-artifacts/eng-runtime/2145001234/; keep individual .nsys-rep bundles <200MB. Scrub logs with `tools/trace_redact.py` before upload.

 dave: Running nsys smoke with this command now:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=tmp/2145001234 --sample=none --duration=45 --capture-range=nvtx
```
Also capturing torch.profiler with schedule and saving `torch_profiler.pth` for ops breakdown.

 mike: For torch.profiler use this snippet so we capture cpu+cuda and call stacks: 
```
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=True, with_stack=True, profile_memory=True, schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=1, active=3)) as prof:
    for batch in dataloader:
        model(batch)
        prof.step()
    prof.export_chrome_trace('torch_trace.json')
```
Make sure to pin seeds and run on a cold VM for the cold-start part.

 dave: got it. Running on rtx-6000-dedicated-3, cold rebooted instance, pinned to CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. First pass done, attaching sizes: `nsys` bundle 128MB gz, torch_trace.json 24MB, torch_profiler.pth 16MB.

 anjali: Awesome — can you upload and paste the link? Also include `nvtx` markers we added around kvcache warmup in the model code.

 dave: Uploaded to https://s3.redwood.internal/perf-artifacts/eng-runtime/2145001234/trace_bundle.tar.gz (public-link disabled). Also uploaded a scrubbed JSON at https://s3.redwood.internal/perf-artifacts/eng-runtime/2145001234/trace_scrubbed.json.

 sara: Thanks! Quick notes: I see a big gap in kernel dispatch for the first 3 tokens; looks like allocator sync on first kv write. Can you also run a tiny variant with `batch=1` and `--no-prefetch` to confirm if batching hides the issue?

 dave: Will run batch=1 next and toggle prefetch flag. ETA 25m.

 perf-bot: Auto-checklist: nsys present, torch.profiler trace present, nvtx markers present, scrubbed=yes, size_ok=yes.

 mike: If the allocator is the culprit, try setting env `TORCH_USE_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` and re-run to see if fragmentation causes the sync. Small experiment but useful.

 anjali: Also file a quick perf issue with links and attach the minimal reproducer (bench/warmup_min_repro.py). Mark it `severity:high` if p99 regression >15%.

 dave: filing issue now and pinging infra to retag the instance for repro. Will paste the issue link when done.

 sara: Perfect — thanks team. If batch=1 confirms, we should consider reverting the allocator change or gating it behind a flag for now.

 dave: Issue created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4321 — includes traces and preliminary graphs.

 sara: Great. I'll start a short canary rollback patch and run the same smoke traces in CI once you give the final green on the repro.

 mike: Happy to review the rollback. :thumbsup:

 anjali: keeping thread open for followups.
